render.what: render a template that is already compiled
render.why: the same work costs fewer microseconds

parse.what: compile a template and render it, in one call
parse.why: the same work costs fewer microseconds

compile.what: compile a template without rendering it
compile.why: the same compile costs fewer microseconds

families.micro: one construct per row, so a regression names itself. It is two families and the earlier note here claimed one: the single-node rows (text, variable, lookup, if, filter, escape) are mostly a measurement of the render call, and the loop, include and extends rows are a measurement of the construct. The call share in the caption says where the split falls on this run
families.real-world: whole pages, rendered by all three engines
families.django-only: the constructs outside the three-engine intersection, rendered by the two engines that have them
families.filters: one illustrative template per default Django filter
families.tags: one illustrative template per builtin Django tag
